name: tui-vpn
tagline: WireGuard and its control plane, from the terminal
description:
WireGuard from the terminal, together with the self-hosted control plane that decides who is allowed onto it.

The status screen reads your interfaces straight from `wg show all dump`: peers, endpoints, the latest handshake, transfer counters, allowed IPs and keepalive. Bringing an interface up or down, adding or removing a peer — every change is shown as the exact command line first and applied only after you confirm it. A private key is never shown, typed, or put on a command line; a pre-shared key is passed to `wg` as a file, never as an argument.

When a [Headscale](https://headscale.net) control plane is present, tui-vpn also reads its users, nodes and pre-authentication keys, and performs the few safe mutations — expire a node, create a user — under the same preview-and-confirm rule. User login is deliberately not in here: identity is OpenID Connect, done in the client's browser against your IdP. The Headscale server exposes no web admin, which is the whole point of the design.

Run it with `--demo` to see every screen against a fake WireGuard and a fake Headscale, with nothing installed. OpenVPN is a planned second backend, not part of this phase.

notes.impact: `preauthkeys list` requires a `--user`, so the pre-auth keys screen may be empty; users and nodes are unaffected

source.command:
git clone https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-vpn
cd tui-vpn && make demo

pacman.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

apt.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

dnf.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

binary.command:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-vpn/releases/download/v{version}/tui-vpn_{version}_linux_{arch}.tar.gz | tar -xz tui-vpn
sudo install -m0755 tui-vpn /usr/local/bin/tui-vpn
binary.note: Available once the first release is tagged.

security.needs_sudo: Reading a WireGuard interface needs CAP_NET_ADMIN and the Headscale CLI talks to a root-owned socket, so reads escalate through the configured prefix; `ip link` does not. Every mutation escalates and is previewed and confirmed first.
